text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The United Nations Development Programme is funding an eight-month $500,000 Vietnamese-American project to study the global application of a drug addiction treatment in Vietnam using herbal medication.
-- Vietnam is expected to earn $100 million per year from tea exports by 2000, the director of Vietnam Tea Corporation said.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet and his wife are scheduled to visit Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Italy and Hungary from May 20 to May 28.
-- The first U.S Ambassador to Vietnam, Douglas "Pete" Peterson, submitted his credentials to Vice President Nguyen Thi Binh on Wednesday.
-- Vietnam's two-week drugs trial ended with eight death sentences and life imprisonment for eight people.
-- Vietnam sold 50 billion dong of one-year Treasury notes at a rate of 12 percent to four domestic institutions and one foreign bank on Wednesday.
-- Vietnam's textile and garment industry is aiming for export turnover of $250 million in the first six months of 1997.

-- Nearly 100 foreign and domestic companies participated in an international four-day exhibition to display machinery, equipments and industrial products which opened in Ho Chi Minh City on Wednesday.
